papers.title_en: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution
papers.authors: Zixuan Wang, Wei Zhang, Chenlei Zhu, Naiyu Chen, Xihua Wang, Jie Chen
papers.evidence: 规划器选择复用技能并按需获取缺失技能以执行具身任务
papers.tldr: 机器人在部分可观测环境中执行任务时，既要消解不确定性，又常缺乏所需技能。CHASE 将好奇心操作化为选择能降低任务不确定性并扩展可执行能力的探究行为，用四个模块串联场景理解、假设驱动规划、按需技能获取与验证执行。规划器权衡信息价值、技能复用与获取执行成本。仿真与真机实验中，在信息与能力双重缺口下任务成功率达 50-80%，证据消解率 70-90%。
papers.abstract_en: Robots executing tasks in partially observed environments must resolve uncertainty while operating with incomplete skills. Inspired by human curiosity, we investigate how robots can formulate task-relevant hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during task execution. We propose CHASE, a Curiosity-guided Harness for Acquiring Skills from Evidence, which operationalizes curiosity as selecting investigations that resolve task uncertainty and expand executable capabilities. Four modules connect dynamic scene understanding, hypothesis-driven planning, on-demand skill acquisition, and verified execution. The planner balances information value, skill reuse, and acquisition/execution cost. Missing skills trigger bounded exploration, learning from verified segments, and held-out admission during acquisition; separate checks verify physical effects and acquired evidence. Newly admitted skills expand the executable investigation set, closing the loop between resolving uncertainty and acquiring capabilities. Simulation and real-robot experiments evaluate investigation, skill acquisition, and task execution. CHASE achieves 50-80% task success under combined information and capability gaps, with 70-90% evidence resolution.

papers.title_en: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
papers.authors: Chenzhi Liu, Jiehong Lin, Wei Huang, Xuzhao Huang, Haoyuan Li, Yang Zhang, Junchao Huang, Chenyeyang Cai, Bo Wang, Kazuhiro Kosuge, Zhongrui Wang, Xiaojuan Qi
papers.evidence: 推理智能体借助机器人控制API求解并把验证方案沉淀为可复用技能供VLA执行
papers.tldr: 机器人需在陌生环境中自主习得并高效执行技能，但VLA策略依赖额外示范，推理智能体反复规划修复成本高。RoboEvo^2提出harness与policy递归协同演化：P2H用策略失败驱动编码智能体搜索Code、Code+ICL、Code+Policy并沉淀可复用技能与经验，H2P用验证轨迹监督训练及反事实偏好蒸馏强化纠错。无需新增人类示范，LIBERO-PRO独立成功率11.0%升至84.1%、混合成功率30.4%升至90.5%，并在RoboTwin C2R与Unitree G1-D验证迁移与95.0%混合成功。
papers.abstract_en: Robots should adapt to unfamiliar environments and acquire new skills through interaction, then execute those skills efficiently with practice. Vision-language-action policies provide efficient control, but often need additional human demonstrations to handle unfamiliar settings; reasoning agents can discover solutions using broad prior knowledge and robot-control APIs, but repeated deliberation and repair are costly. Inspired by human learning through reasoning and practice, we propose RoboEvo$^2$, a framework for recursive harness-policy co-evolution. In Policy-to-Harness (P2H) evolution, policy failures guide a coding agent to search complementary Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes, consolidating verified solutions into reusable skills, routing strategies, and experience memory. In Harness-to-Policy (H2P) evolution, verified trajectories provide supervised training, while Counterfactual Preference Distillation (CPD) teaches the policy to favor successful corrections over failures from the same starting state. The improved policy provides stronger motor skills for subsequent search, while its remaining failures redirect harness evolution, closing the reciprocal loop. Through recursive co-evolution without additional human demonstrations, RoboEvo$^2$ improves standalone success from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5% on LIBERO-PRO, with similar gains and reduced agentic costs on RoboTwin C2R. Further experiments demonstrate autonomous task acquisition, cross-embodiment harness transfer, and 95.0% hybrid success on the Unitree G1-D. Our models and code will be publicly released.

papers.title_en: RePlan-VLA: Progress-Aware Replanning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Apoorva Vashisth, Manav Kulshrestha, Damon Conover, Zachary Kingston, Aniket Bera
papers.evidence: 面向长时程机器人执行的VLA策略进度感知重规划框架
papers.tldr: 长程机器人操作常涉及多步相互依赖，VLA模型因同时承担长程推理、记忆、动作生成与纠错而性能下降。RePlan-VLA将底层VLA视为短程操作器，显式监测机器人运动以评估进度，并根据执行结果自适应修正未来计划。框架与具体VLA解耦且无需额外微调，在RoboCasa365和CALVIN上成功率分别提升21.9%与10.4%，并完成Franka Research 3实机验证。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation, yet their performance often degrades on long-horizon tasks that require multiple interdependent manipulations. Instead of burdening the VLA policies with long-horizon reasoning, memory, action generation, progress tracking, and error recovery, we argue for leveraging their short-horizon manipulation capabilities within an execution-aware framework. To this end, we introduce \textnormal{\textbf{RePlan-VLA}}, a VLA-agnostic framework that translates a VLA's short-horizon capabilities into reliable long-horizon execution. RePlan-VLA explicitly monitors the robot's motion for progress evaluation, and adaptively revises the future plan based on observed outcomes. We preserve the underlying VLA policy entirely, requiring no additional fine-tuning. Experiments on RoboCasa365 and CALVIN benchmarks show an improvement of 21.9% and 10.4% in success rate over the next strongest baseline. We also validate our approach for real-world deployment on a Franka Research 3 robot.

papers.title_en: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
papers.authors: Chenyuan Zhou, Chaoyi Huang, Zibo Wang, Zhiyuan Li, Yong-Lu Li
papers.evidence: 具身智能体提出假设并调用VLA策略执行工具操作
papers.tldr: 跨工具操作要求理解工具几何与任务功能的关联并调整策略，而新工具的可供性往往难以发现。A^2-VLA把工具可供性视为智能体可构建、测试和修订的假设，先在仿真中重建场景，通过自主实验提取功能区域及其几何特征，形成可复用技能库，并将编码特征作为π0.5主干的条件输入。在模拟跨工具轨迹重定向中达到86.1%成功率，在三个真实机器人工具使用任务上较π0.5提升30.7个百分点。该工作为未见工具的策略适应提供了可供性发现与验证框架。
papers.abstract_en: Tools with different shapes can have similar functions, but transferring manipulation skills across tools requires understanding how tool geometry relates to the specific task and adjusting the manipulation strategy accordingly. The key challenge is to discover the common affordances that contribute to task completion across different tools and verify whether they support new tools in performing similar work. We present A$^2$-VLA, a tool-adaptation framework that combines an embodied agent with a VLA policy. It treats tool affordances as hypotheses the agent can construct, test, and revise. Given teleoperated demonstrations with a few source tools, the agent reconstructs the scenes in simulation and autonomously determines task-relevant affordance features: functional regions and their key geometric properties. It develops affordance-extraction skills and refines both the features and skills through autonomous experiments in the reconstructed scenes. Validated extraction skills accumulate in a reusable skill library for unseen tools. Finally, A$^2$-VLA uses encoded functional-region features as conditioning inputs to a $π_{0.5}$ backbone during training and inference. Evaluation examines affordance reliability in reconstructed scenes and real-robot task success on unseen tools. Our method achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting based on affordances. On three real-robot tool-use tasks, A$^2$-VLA improves task success by 30.7 percentage points over $π_{0.5}$.

papers.title_en: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Zhenxuan Fan, Zhuoya Wang, Yuqian Yuan, Wenqiao Zhang, Juncheng Li, Jun Xiao, Siliang Tang, Yueting Zhuang
papers.evidence: 双智能体框架中Actor通过机器人控制接口与视觉语言模型引导交互
papers.tldr: 针对VLM机器人操作智能体在记忆组织、失败归因和执行经验复用上的不足，Embodied-Harness提出双智能体框架，在不更新模型参数的情况下迭代优化执行harness。Actor通过机器人控制接口与环境交互，Reflector将执行证据转化为可复用操作指导，并借助分层记忆与递归自我改进支撑多次尝试。方法在三个仿真基准取得82.4%、76.7%、94.4%成功率，真实三任务平均96.7%，展现经验驱动的操作能力提升潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Embodied-Harness in generalization under environmental variations, spatial reasoning, long-horizon planning, and memory-dependent manipulation. Our method achieves success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on the three benchmarks, respectively. Real-world evaluation further yields an average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. These results highlight the potential of Embodied-Harness to improve robotic manipulation through experience-driven harness self-improvement.

papers.title_en: Any2Act: Scaling In-Context Robot Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrations
papers.authors: Ziang Ren, Zifan Wang, Zhuoyang Li, Benhao Qin, Haoyang Li, Qingtao Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi, He Wang, Yanchao Yang, Li Yi
papers.evidence: 大模型低频指定任务，交由上下文机器人策略高频执行
papers.tldr: 机器人上下文学习需从演示中完成未见任务且免微调，但现有方法受限于人机配对稀缺或演示来源单一、规模有限。Any2Act 将演示统一表示为执行机器人的相机布局与动作空间，先从120万条真实机器人轨迹学习跟随，再用少量源路由适配器吸收人视频、仿真、UMI等来源差异。仅凭单条演示，它在未见任务上达到57.5%成功率，超过每任务用50条演示微调的VLA，并让其他演示源保留74%至91%的成功率。
papers.abstract_en: Robot in-context learning (ICL) enables a policy to perform unseen tasks by following contextual demonstrations, without task-specific fine-tuning. This is increasingly valuable as large language models reasoning at low frequency can specify tasks through demonstrations and delegate high-frequency execution to such a policy. However, methods conditioned on human videos are bounded by scarce human-robot pairs, while those conditioned on robot demonstrations accept only one or two source types at limited scale. We present Any2Act, a foundation model for robot ICL. Our key insight is that a demonstration should be expressed in the camera layout and action space of the robot that performs it (the executor), not of whoever provided it (the demonstrator). This unified embodiment-grounded representation decouples learning to follow from admitting a new source. Any2Act learns to follow once, from robot-to-robot pairs that already take this form in 1.2M real trajectories spanning 10K tasks. Human videos, simulation, UMI, and other robots are then translated into this representation, and source-routed adapters trained on only a few hundred pairs each absorb the residual gap while the pretrained model stays frozen. For long horizons, a training-free tracker feeds only the demonstration window around the executor's progress, bounding the context and rolling back to redo failed steps. From a single demonstration, Any2Act achieves 57.5% success on unseen tasks without fine-tuning, exceeding VLAs fine-tuned on 50 demonstrations per task; other demonstrators retain 74-91% of the success achieved with the executor's own demonstrations.
